content.title: Is This Terrifying Face of Nature a Mere Coincidence, or a Warning from Our Lord?
content.subtitle: A Call to Seek Shelter Under the Lord's Mercy in This Era of Worldwide Calamities
content.body:
Over the past few years, the entire world has borne cruel witness to one natural disaster after another. In September 2024, unprecedented heavy rainfall and catastrophic landslides in Nepal claimed over 250 lives, leaving thousands of families homeless. Prior to that, in early 2023, a massive 7.8-magnitude earthquake in Turkey and Syria snuffed out more than 60,000 precious lives in the blink of an eye, reducing entire cities to rubble. In the same year, the collapse of dams caused by Storm Daniel in Libya swept away over 4,500 people, while an earthquake in Morocco wiped out numerous mountain settlements. Even close to us, frequent tremors, unexpected floods, and hill landslides constantly point out humanity’s extreme vulnerability.

The Burden of Sins and Clear Warnings from the Quran and Hadith

In the Holy Quran, Almighty Allah has unequivocally stated the underlying reason behind such worldwide calamities:

“Corruption has appeared throughout the land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned, so that He may let them taste part of [the consequence of] what they have done that perhaps they will return [to the right path].”

— (Surah Ar-Rum: 41)

In the Noble Hadith, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ explicitly warned that the shaking of the earth or sudden disasters are not merely geographical events. He stated that when musical instruments and intoxicants become commonplace, adultery and immorality spread openly, and people regard sin as trivial, it is then that frequent massive earthquakes, landslides, and sudden disasters will proliferate (Jami` at-Tirmidhi: 2211). Every calamity is a glaring warning sign born of our sins, prompting us to rectify ourselves while there is still time.

The Infallible Shield Against Calamity: Tawbah and Istighfar

The greatest protective barrier against Allah’s punishment and wrath is constant ‘Istighfar’. In the Holy Quran, Almighty Allah Himself offers reassurance:

“And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would He punish them while they seek forgiveness.”

— (Surah Al-Anfal: 33)

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ elaborated that whoever firmly adheres to Istighfar as a constant habit, Allah creates a way out from every distress, relieves all anxieties, and grants sustenance from sources unimaginable (Sunan Abi Dawud: 1518).

An Easy Way to Cling to Forgiveness Amid a Busy Life

Yet, in the relentless rush of worldly responsibilities and the nonstop day-and-night hustle, our time flies so fast that, despite our good intentions, we barely find the opportunity to repent for our mistakes a few times a day. Amid your continuous busy life, Muslims Day can serve as your constant companion for good deeds.

The app's Istighfar Reminder feature will gently bring you back to the threshold of your Lord's forgiveness at regular intervals throughout your busy schedule. Even when your phone is in silent mode, it will signal you with a gentle vibration—ensuring that amidst thousands of tasks, the practice of Istighfar remains alive on your lips, even if only for a few moments.
